Wielkie Oczy Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wielkie Oczy, Poland

Not demolished. Wielkie Oczy's Jewish community, present from the town's founding in 1671, numbered 386 people by 1765, declining to 560 (29 percent of the town) by 1939. This cemetery was likely established in the late 17th century. During WWII, executions and unmarked mass burials, now symbolically commemorated, took place at the site; in 1942, tombstones were plundered by townspeople for construction, leaving only about 30 matzevot in their original locations. At the start of the 21st century, the site was cleaned and refenced, and recovered tombstones from the town and surrounding area were gradually returned. About 200 tombstones survive today, the oldest dated 1759 and the newest 1941.
